articles.title: Two Unpatched Citrix NetScaler RCE Zero-Days Under Active Exploitation
articles.executive_summary: Two unpatched zero-day vulnerabilities in Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway appliances are being actively exploited, allowing remote code execution. Citrix has not confirmed the flaws or published a fix, prompting some administrators to take appliances offline.
articles.technical_breakdown: The vulnerabilities allow remote code execution through unspecified attack vectors, with Citrix appliances being taken offline to prevent exploitation. The root cause of the issue is the presence of unpatched zero-day vulnerabilities in Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway appliances.
actionable_mitigations: Take Citrix appliances offline to prevent exploitation
Implement network segmentation and isolation
Monitor for suspicious activity and implement detection and log monitoring indicators
articles.telegram_snippet: Two unpatched Citrix NetScaler zero-day vulnerabilities are being actively exploited, allowing remote code execution. Citrix has not confirmed the flaws or published a fix, prompting some administrators to take appliances offline.

articles.title: ShinyHunters uses WAF bypass trick in Oracle PeopleSoft attacks
articles.executive_summary: The ShinyHunters extortion gang is exploiting the Oracle PeopleSoft CVE-2026-35273 flaw to gain unauthorized access to vulnerable servers. This attack vector poses a significant operational risk to affected organizations.
articles.technical_breakdown: The attackers are using a URL-encoding trick to bypass web application firewall rules, allowing them to exploit the CVE-2026-35273 flaw on vulnerable servers. This exploitation mechanics leverages a previously unknown vulnerability in the WAF rules.
actionable_mitigations: Apply the patch for CVE-2026-35273 as soon as possible
Review and update WAF rules to prevent the URL-encoding trick
Monitor for suspicious activity and implement detection and log monitoring indicators
articles.telegram_snippet: ShinyHunters gang resumes Oracle PeopleSoft attacks using WAF bypass trick, exploiting CVE-2026-35273 flaw on vulnerable servers. Affected organizations must apply the patch and update WAF rules immediately.

articles.title: Attackers Bypass WAFs to Exploit Oracle PeopleSoft Flaw and Deploy Web Shells
articles.executive_summary: Attackers are exploiting a critical security vulnerability in Oracle PeopleSoft to deploy web shells, bypassing WAFs and targeting multiple sectors globally. The vulnerability, CVE-2026-35273, has a CVSS score of 9.8 and allows unauthenticated remote code execution.
articles.technical_breakdown: The vulnerability, CVE-2026-35273, is being weaponized by attackers to gain unauthenticated remote code execution, allowing them to deploy web shells and bypass WAFs. The exploitation mechanics involve targeting the known security flaw in Oracle PeopleSoft.
actionable_mitigations: Apply the latest patch for Oracle PeopleSoft to address CVE-2026-35273
Implement network containment and firewall rules to block suspicious traffic
Monitor logs for indicators of exploitation, such as unusual HTTP requests
articles.telegram_snippet: Attackers are exploiting a critical Oracle PeopleSoft flaw (CVE-2026-35273) to deploy web shells, bypassing WAFs and targeting multiple sectors globally. Apply the latest patch and monitor logs for suspicious activity.

articles.title: Lunex Stealer Abuses AMD Driver to Disable Security Monitoring and Steal Browser Credentials
articles.executive_summary: Lunex Stealer Abuses AMD Driver to Disable Security Monitoring and Steal Browser Credentials. The Psychedelic Stealer malware distributed via compromised Ukrainian websites using ClickFix-style Cloudflare verification checks is part of a wider malware-as-a-service (MaaS) platform called Lunex.
articles.technical_breakdown: Analysis of incident reported by The Hacker News. The threat involves attack vectors targeting standard services. Further technical telemetry is developing.

articles.title: Microsoft pauses KB5002907 update after Office license deactivations
articles.executive_summary: Microsoft has paused the rollout of the KB5002907 update after users reported that it deactivated or removed perpetual Office 2016 and Office 2019 installations. This issue poses a significant operational risk to organizations relying on these Office versions.
articles.technical_breakdown: The KB5002907 update appears to have triggered a licensing issue, causing Office 2016 and Office 2019 installations to be deactivated or removed. The root cause is likely related to the update's interaction with Microsoft's licensing mechanisms.
actionable_mitigations: Do not install the KB5002907 update until further notice
Verify Office license status before applying updates
Monitor for similar licensing issues with other Microsoft updates
articles.telegram_snippet: Microsoft pauses KB5002907 update after reports of Office license deactivations. Organizations should refrain from installing the update until further notice.

articles.title: GitHub Actions re-enabled with Mini Shai-Hulud payload still active
articles.executive_summary: Two compromised GitHub Actions were re-enabled, allowing malicious code to remain accessible for over a week, posing a risk to users who may have inadvertently downloaded the payload. This incident highlights the importance of monitoring third-party dependencies for potential security vulnerabilities.
articles.technical_breakdown: The Mini Shai-Hulud campaign compromised two GitHub Actions, which were later re-enabled, allowing the malicious code to remain active. The malicious code was likely exploited through the use of third-party dependencies, emphasizing the need for thorough dependency monitoring.
actionable_mitigations: Verify the integrity of third-party dependencies
Monitor GitHub Actions for suspicious activity
Implement regular security audits for dependencies
articles.telegram_snippet: Compromised GitHub Actions re-enabled, allowing malicious code to remain accessible for over a week, posing a risk to users.

articles.title: New x47.c Windows Botnet Weaponizes xAI Grok, AI API Draining
articles.executive_summary: A new Windows botnet leverages AI to maintain persistence, posing a significant threat to enterprise networks. The botnet's use of xAI Grok API draining enables it to choose from predefined actions, increasing its operational risk.
articles.technical_breakdown: The botnet relies on AI to select from predefined actions, utilizing xAI Grok to maintain persistence. This AI-driven approach allows the botnet to adapt and evade detection.
actionable_mitigations: Implement xAI Grok API restrictions and monitoring
Enforce strict network segmentation and access controls
Monitor for suspicious AI-driven activity and implement detection and response measures
articles.telegram_snippet: New Windows botnet leverages AI to maintain persistence, using xAI Grok API draining to choose from predefined actions, posing a significant threat to enterprise networks.

articles.title: US and China Agree to Establish AI Safety Channel
articles.executive_summary: The US and China have agreed to establish a communication mechanism for AI-related incidents, aiming to prevent potential security risks. This move is part of ongoing trade and military talks between the two nations.
articles.technical_breakdown: The agreement focuses on setting up a channel for reporting and addressing AI-related incidents, with the goal of preventing potential security risks. The exact technical details of the mechanism are not publicly disclosed.

Establish clear communication channels with international partners for AI-related incident reporting

articles.title: Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 AI Writing Patterns Evolve
articles.executive_summary: Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 AI writing patterns have evolved to use fewer obvious AI writing patterns, resulting in shorter sentences and simpler wording. This change may indicate an improvement in AI writing capabilities.
articles.technical_breakdown: Analysis of Claude Opus 5.5's writing shows a reduction in em dashes and an increase in sentence complexity, suggesting a shift in AI writing mechanics. The root cause of this change is attributed to improvements in AI training data and algorithms.
articles.telegram_snippet: Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 AI writing patterns have evolved, using fewer obvious AI patterns and simpler wording, indicating potential improvements in AI writing capabilities.
